row.title: Conditional weak convergence in probability
row.statement:
Let $E$ be a separable complete metric space, let $\mathcal D_n$ be the sigma-algebra generated by the observed data at sample size $n$, and let $Z_n^*$ be a bootstrap random element whose remaining randomness is the resampling randomization. Write $\mathcal L^*(Z_n^*)$ for its conditional Borel probability law given $\mathcal D_n$. Supply as part of the data a metric $d_w$ on Borel probability measures on $E$ such that $d_w(\mu_n,\mu)\to0$ exactly when $\mu_n\Rightarrow\mu$ in the sense of [[def-weak-convergence-of-borel-probability-measures]]. Assume the displayed metric distance is a measurable real random variable. For a fixed Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $E$, we say that $Z_n^*$ converges conditionally weakly in probability to $\mu$ when

$$d_w\!\left(\mathcal L^*(Z_n^*),\mu\right)\longrightarrow 0\quad\hbox{in probability}.$$

The metric is supplied as a hypothesis; this definition makes no metric-existence assertion. It applies to separable complete metric spaces, including separable Banach spaces, their closed linear subspaces and finite products.
row.strategy: Operational definition; no phase proof is applicable.

references.title: D. Pilavakis, E. Paparoditis, and T. Sapatinas, Moving block and tapered block bootstrap for functional time series with an application to the K-sample mean problem, Bernoulli 25 (2019), Section 2.2, Theorem 2.1

row.title: Conditional bootstrap delta method for Hadamard differentiable maps
row.statement:
Let $E,F$ be separable Banach spaces, $E_0\subseteq E$ a closed linear subspace, $\theta\in E$, and $D\subseteq E$ a neighbourhood of $\theta$. Let $t_n>0$ decrease to zero, let $Z_n\in E_0$ be data-measurable and tight, and let $Z_n^*\in E_0$ be bootstrap random elements such that $\theta+t_nZ_n$ and $\theta+t_n(Z_n+Z_n^*)$ lie in $D$ with probability tending to one. Supply weak-convergence metrics on probability laws on $E_0$ and $F$ as in [[def-conditional-weak-convergence-in-probability]], with measurable distances for the conditional laws below. Assume:

1. $\mathcal L^*(Z_n^*)$ converges conditionally weakly in probability to the fixed law of $G\in E_0$, as in [[def-conditional-weak-convergence-in-probability]];
2. $Z_n^*$ is conditionally tight in probability: for each $\epsilon,\eta>0$, there is a deterministic compact $K\subset E_0$ such that $\limsup_n\Pr\{\Pr^*(Z_n^*\notin K)>\epsilon\}<\eta$;
3. $D$ is Borel and $\Psi:D\to F$ is Borel measurable and Hadamard differentiable at $\theta$, tangentially to $E_0$, with continuous linear derivative $\Psi'_\theta$ as in [[def-hadamard-differentiability-tangentially]].

Then

$$\mathcal L^*\!\left(t_n^{-1}\{\Psi(\theta+t_n(Z_n+Z_n^*))-\Psi(\theta+t_nZ_n)\}\right)$$

converges conditionally weakly in probability to the law of $\Psi'_\theta(G)$. Define the displayed bootstrap difference to be $0\in F$ whenever either argument lies outside $D$; the assumed vanishing probability of this event makes this convention asymptotically immaterial.

references.title: D. Pilavakis, E. Paparoditis, and T. Sapatinas, Moving block and tapered block bootstrap for functional time series with an application to the K-sample mean problem, Bernoulli 25 (2019), Remark 2.1

row.title: Conditional K-sample block-bootstrap validity under a joint CLT
row.statement:
Let $H$ be a real separable Hilbert space. Fix $K\ge2$. Let $Y_{i,1},\ldots,Y_{i,n_i}\in H$, $1\le i\le K$, be independent functional time-series samples, $M=\sum_i n_i\to\infty$, and suppose $n_i/M\to\theta_i\in(0,1)$. Under the null hypothesis $\mu_1=\cdots=\mu_K=\mu$, let $\bar Y_i$ be the sample means and let $\bar Y_P=M^{-1}\sum_i n_i\bar Y_i$. Apply [[alg-k-sample-null-constrained-block-bootstrap]] to these observations with integer block lengths $1\le b_i\le n_i$ for every sample size used and a specified moving or tapered mode. In tapered mode supply the admissible windows and strictly positive block norms required by [[alg-tapered-block-bootstrap]] at each $b_i$. Draw the starts conditionally independently across series and blocks, and write $\bar Y_i^*$ for the resulting pseudo-series means.

Assume the original centered mean vector

$$U_M=\bigl(\sqrt{n_i}(\bar Y_i-\mu)\bigr)_{i=1}^K$$

converges weakly to a joint law $\mathcal L(G_1,\ldots,G_K)$, and assume the conditional law of

$$U_M^*=\bigl(\sqrt{n_i}(\bar Y_i^*-\bar Y_P)\bigr)_{i=1}^K$$

converges conditionally weakly in probability to that same joint law and is conditionally tight in probability: for every $\epsilon,\eta>0$ there is a deterministic compact $C\subset H^K$ such that $\limsup_M\Pr\{\Pr^*(U_M^*\notin C)>\epsilon\}<\eta$. These are explicit joint-limit hypotheses; this theorem does not derive them from the MBB or TBB conditions.

Define the contrast maps

$$L_M(z_1,\ldots,z_K)=\bigl(\sqrt{M/n_i}\,z_i-\sqrt{M/n_K}\,z_K\bigr)_{i=1}^{K-1},\qquad L_\theta(z)=\bigl(z_i/\sqrt{\theta_i}-z_K/\sqrt{\theta_K}\bigr)_{i=1}^{K-1}.$$

For every continuous $\Psi:H^{K-1}\to S$ into a metric space $S$, the conditional law of $\Psi(L_MU_M^*)$ converges testwise in probability to the law of $\Psi(L_\theta(G_1,\ldots,G_K))$: for every bounded continuous $f:S\to\mathbb R$, the corresponding conditional expectation tends in probability to $E f(\Psi(L_\theta(G_1,\ldots,G_K)))$. If $S$ is separable and complete and a weak-convergence metric with measurable conditional distances is supplied, the conclusion is also conditional weak convergence in probability in the sense of [[def-conditional-weak-convergence-in-probability]]. Under the null, the sampling law of $\Psi(L_MU_M)$ has the same limit. The maps may be squared norms, integrated linear contrasts, or any other continuous statistic of this scaled contrast.
row.strategy: contrast the common null location, apply the joint conditional limit, and use the continuous mapping theorem

row.title: Conditional CLT for independent resampled weighted blocks
row.statement:
Assume AC and all the process and weight hypotheses of [[lem-weighted-overlapping-block-moment-and-covariance-limits]], including squared normalization and convergence of each fixed-lag weight autocorrelation to one. Let $b=b_n\to\infty$ with $b/\sqrt n\to0$, $N=n-b+1$, $k=\lfloor n/b\rfloor$, $r=n-kb$, and

$$B_{j,q}=\sum_{\ell=1}^q c_{b,\ell}X_{j+\ell-1},\qquad \bar B_q=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^NB_{j,q},\qquad C_q=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^N(B_{j,q}-\bar B_q)\otimes(B_{j,q}-\bar B_q),$$

with $B_{j,0}=\bar B_0=C_0=0$. Conditional on the observations choose independent uniform starts $J_1,\ldots,J_{k+1}$ in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ and set

$$Z_n^*=n^{-1/2}\left\{\sum_{s=1}^k(B_{J_s,b}-\bar B_b)+(B_{J_{k+1},r}-\bar B_r)\right\}.$$

Then, for the centered Hilbert Gaussian $G$ of covariance $\Gamma$,

$$\mathcal L^*(Z_n^*)\Rightarrow\mathcal L(G)\quad\hbox{in probability},\qquad \left\|\operatorname{Cov}^*(Z_n^*)-\Gamma\right\|_1\longrightarrow0\quad\hbox{in probability}.$$

Trace-norm convergence implies convergence in Hilbert-Schmidt norm as well. The conditional laws are tight in probability: for every $\varepsilon,\eta>0$ there is a deterministic compact $K\subset H$ such that $\limsup_nP\{P^*(Z_n^*\notin K)>\varepsilon\}<\eta$. The complete blocks satisfy conditional Lindeberg, and the final partial block has $E E^*\|n^{-1/2}(B_{J_{k+1},r}-\bar B_r)\|^2=O(b/n)$. Replacing every $X_t$ by $X_t-M_n$ for any common data-dependent $M_n\in H$ leaves $Z_n^*$ and all its conditional covariances unchanged.
row.strategy: uniform integrability, conditional characteristic functions, projection tails and a negligible partial block

references.title: D. Pilavakis, E. Paparoditis, and T. Sapatinas, Moving block and tapered block bootstrap for functional time series with an application to the K-sample mean problem, Bernoulli 25 (2019), proof of Theorem 2.1; weighted-block and arbitrary-length extension proved locally
